deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It holds three drafts in Riemann's hand.

(1) Family letter, end of 1853. The addressee is probably his father, since the letter is a birthday letter and later mentions his siblings. Riemann apologises for not writing because he could not yet report that his Habilitationsschrift was finished. It has now been handed in, and he is to hold the colloquium in the next few days. For the trial lecture he had to propose three topics. He had worked out the first (an interlinear insertion suggests the first two) and hoped one of these would be chosen. Gauss instead chose the third, 'über die Hypothesen, welche der Geometrie zu Grunde liegen', and Riemann is 'in der Klemme' because he still has to work it out. The colloquium will probably be the next Tuesday or Thursday. He sends birthday wishes. He says other work has progressed far enough that he needs no books, and asks to come home for 6-8 weeks to recover from an earlier illness and to save costs. This matches the well-known passage quoted in Dedekind's biography of Riemann (letter of late December 1853), so it dates the folio to about December 1853 / early 1854.

(2) The opening of a second family letter, 'Liebe Ida(?)' (his sister Ida), thanking her for a letter. It breaks off.

(3) Draft of a formal letter to a 'Hochgeschätzter Herr Professor'. Riemann refers to the kind reception of his 'jüngsten Versuche' and to a theory of the 'Rückstand'. He asks that his results be taken not as definitive but as a further working-out of the addressee's results. The topic is the residual charge of the Leyden jar. This strongly suggests the 1854 correspondence with Rudolf Kohlrausch about Riemann's theory of the electric residue. The next page continues this letter, mentioning Pfingsten and Quickborn, together with heat-conduction (erfc / Fourier series) formulas.

There is no derivation to reconstruct. The mathematics on the neighbouring pages (an operator identity on the previous page; the cooling formula chi_t = chi_0*(8/pi^2)*sum exp(-(2n+1)^2*pi^2*beta^2*t/(4*alpha*a^2))/(2n+1)^2 on the next) is not on this folio.

results.what: Biographical: Gauss chose the third proposed topic, 'Über die Hypothesen, welche der Geometrie zu Grunde liegen', for Riemann's Habilitation lecture; Riemann had prepared the other topic(s).
results.modern_name: Riemann's Habilitationsvortrag (1854), origin of Riemannian geometry
results.usually_credited_to: Known from Riemann's letter quoted by Dedekind (1876 biography)

results.what: Draft letter to a professor (very likely R. Kohlrausch) offering Riemann's theory of the electric residue ('Rückstand') as a further development of the addressee's experimental results.
results.modern_name: Riemann's theory of the residual charge in the Leyden jar (1854)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (paper printed in the Gesammelte Werke)

deep.surprise_reason: The page consists of letter drafts. The Gauss/Habilitation episode is famous and already published through Dedekind's biography. The Kohlrausch/Rückstand correspondence is known. The only point of interest is that this is a draft version showing variant wording and that it dates the folio's context to around December 1853 - spring 1854.
transcription_corrections: The salutation is likely 'Lieber Vater!' (a birthday letter mentioning 'meine Geschwister'), but this is uncertain from the image.
The interlinear insertion before 'hatte ich ausgearbeitet' probably reads 'die beiden ersten' or similar, consistent with Dedekind's quotation that the first two topics were prepared.
'zum Theil des Rückstandes' is likely '(zur) Theorie des Rückstandes', referring to the electric residue (Kohlrausch).
'Riemann 9' at top left is an archival/foliation mark, not part of the text.
The second letter fragment's salutation 'Liebe Ida' (Riemann's sister) appears plausible.
